claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy has a single-phase dendritic BCC structure.
The initial dendritic microstructure is produced by conventional casting and solidification.
The untreated TiVNbTa alloy has an approximately 330 MPa yield strength at 1273 K.
The untreated TiVNbTa alloy has an approximately 423 MPa compressive strength at 1273 K.
A solutionizing treatment will homogenize the TiVNbTa microstructure.
A subsequent aging treatment below 1273 K will induce nanoscale coherent precipitates in the BCC matrix.
The induced precipitates will remain thermally stable at 1273 K.
An aging temperature of approximately 900–1050 K is proposed for precipitate formation.
The desired treated microstructure is a fine dispersion of nanoscale coherent precipitates within the BCC matrix.
The nanoscale precipitates will act as pinning obstacles to dislocations.
The precipitates will hinder both dislocation glide and dislocation climb.
Hindering dislocation glide and climb will retard high-temperature deformation at 1273 K.
The two-step heat treatment will significantly increase yield strength at 1273 K relative to the approximately 330 MPa baseline.
The two-step heat treatment will maintain or modestly enhance compressive strength at 1273 K relative to the untreated alloy.
The proposed intervention is applicable to an intermediate layer operating between W and CuCrZr.
The relevant mechanical comparison is compression testing at 1273 K using the same strain rate and loading conditions for treated and baseline specimens.
